Module: ## LAUNCH BLOCKERS — P0 — must be closed before a production release

Scenario: Persisted state blob is unparseable JSON after a partial write or manual edit
Expected Behavior: Discard the corrupt key and boot from a clean initial state within the same launch. Never enter a crash loop. Surface a one-time 'we could not restore your data' notice rather than failing silently.

Scenario: Persisted blob carries a valid schemaVersion but a structurally invalid body
Expected Behavior: Validate the actual shape on every read rather than trusting the version field. Reject the payload and fall back to a clean state.

Scenario: User stored mid-flow on the retired 'gender' onboarding step is upgraded from schema v1
Expected Behavior: Migrate the step to 'details' so a phone-verified user resumes at the correct screen. Never route a verified user back to step one.

Scenario: Device storage read throws because storage is locked or unavailable
Expected Behavior: Raise a typed storage error. Render a recoverable boot error screen with a retry action. Never throw an unhandled exception through the render tree.

Scenario: Storage write fails because the device is out of space
Expected Behavior: Reject the mutation with a typed storage error and tell the user the action did not persist. Never report success for a write that did not land.

Scenario: App is deleted and reinstalled after a long streak
Expected Behavior: All state is device-local with no cloud backup, so a reinstall is a total loss of streak, contributions and Future You progress. Disclose this in onboarding and the logout dialog, and gate launch on a server-side account or an explicit export.

Scenario: Personally identifiable data is written to device storage in plaintext
Expected Behavior: Phone number, name and age must be stored in encrypted storage (Keychain or EncryptedSharedPreferences) rather than AsyncStorage before any production release.

Scenario: Storage is tampered with on a rooted or jailbroken device to inflate a streak
Expected Behavior: Streak, contribution and reward state must be authoritative server-side. Treat the local copy as a cache. Reject any client-supplied streak value on sync.

Scenario: Two devices sign in with the same number and write divergent local state
Expected Behavior: Resolve to a single server-authoritative record on sync using a deterministic rule such as union of contributions by day index. Never silently discard the losing device's contributions.

Scenario: A non-finite value reaches a currency label from a division or a corrupted restore
Expected Behavior: Clamp non-finite values to zero at the formatter so 'NaN' or 'Infinity' can never render on a money surface.

Scenario: Projection inputs contain NaN or Infinity
Expected Behavior: Substitute a safe fallback for every non-finite input before computing. Every emitted point and every summary figure must be finite.

Scenario: Chart requests a value from an empty projection series before data lands
Expected Behavior: Return zero rather than dereferencing an undefined index.

Scenario: Withdrawal lever exceeds total holdings
Expected Behavior: Cap the withdrawal at the available balance. The curve starts at zero and no point in the series is negative.

Scenario: Full liquidation drives the invested total below zero
Expected Behavior: Floor the invested total at zero so capital contributed never renders as a negative figure.

Scenario: A negative assumed rate is applied across a long horizon
Expected Behavior: Floor the balance at zero at every point. This product does not model a portfolio that owes money.

Scenario: Borrow request exceeds the 50 percent loan-to-value ceiling
Expected Behavior: Reject with a non-retryable limit error carrying the requested and available amounts. Do not render a retry affordance for a request that can never succeed.

Scenario: Portfolio value falls after a loan is taken so remaining capacity computes negative
Expected Behavior: Clamp available capacity at zero. Never present a negative borrowing offer.

Scenario: Borrow submitted with an amount of zero or below
Expected Behavior: Reject at the API boundary with a validation error before any loan record is written.

Scenario: Hold-to-invest gesture is released before the charge completes
Expected Behavior: Cancel the pending commit so no contribution is written and no money moves. Drain the charge indicator to zero.

Scenario: Commit response is lost after the change was accepted server-side and the user retries
Expected Behavior: Reuse the idempotency key minted before the first attempt so the server returns the original result. One SIP change must never be booked twice.

Scenario: SIP change is presented as successful before the write is confirmed
Expected Behavior: Advance to the success screen only after the commit resolves. Never confirm optimistically on a financial mutation.

Scenario: An unexpected exception escapes a request handler
Expected Behavior: Normalise anything thrown into a typed API error so the UI never receives a raw exception.

Scenario: Local queue and server disagree after reconnect because both changed while offline
Expected Behavior: Define and implement a conflict policy before launch: server wins for balances and SIP, union-by-day for contributions. Present any discarded local change to the user rather than dropping it silently.

Scenario: Sync completes for some entities and fails for others
Expected Behavior: Apply sync transactionally per entity and record per-entity sync state. Never leave the UI showing a partially reconciled portfolio without an explicit 'partially synced' indicator.

Scenario: OTP screen is reached with no phone number in state via a deep link or cleared storage
Expected Behavior: Redirect to the phone step and reject the verify call at the API boundary. The user must never reach a dead-end form.

Scenario: Phone number is persisted to disk but absent from the in-memory store
Expected Behavior: Fold the updated session into the store as part of the OTP challenge response so the next screen's guard does not bounce the user backwards.

Scenario: The hard-coded mock OTP is present in a production build
Expected Behavior: Remove the mock code path and the on-screen code hint from any release build. Gate behind a build-time flag and fail the release pipeline if the constant is reachable.

Scenario: App has no re-authentication on relaunch
Expected Behavior: Require a biometric or PIN unlock before exposing balances, contributions or borrowing capacity in a production build.

Scenario: A user invites their own number or redeems their own invite code
Expected Behavior: Reject self-referral at the point of redemption by comparing the normalised inviter and invitee numbers. Do not credit either side.

Scenario: The same invitee is submitted against a code more than once
Expected Behavior: Enforce a uniqueness constraint on invitee identity per programme so a referral is credited exactly once regardless of retries.

Scenario: Referral rewards are shown as earned but never credited to the balance
Expected Behavior: Either credit the reward to the portfolio on tier completion or label the tier as pending fulfilment. Never display an earned reward the user cannot receive.

Scenario: Logout is triggered by thumb momentum after scrolling the menu
Expected Behavior: Separate the destructive row with a divider and require an explicit confirmation before any data is cleared.

Scenario: Logout wipes device-local data with no server-side account to restore from
Expected Behavior: State plainly in the confirmation that streak, contributions and Future You live on this device and will be cleared. Do not imply the session can be restored.

Scenario: A detail route is opened by deep link with no navigation history behind it
Expected Behavior: Every back control resolves to an explicit fallback route so the user can never be stranded on a screen with no exit.

Scenario: A native capture module is absent from the runtime client
Expected Behavior: Import the native module lazily inside the handler so a missing module fails locally and degrades to a text share. A module-scope import takes the entire navigator down.

Scenario: Demo time travel and streak simulation controls are reachable in a production build
Expected Behavior: Strip all demo controls, the dev menu and the day-offset API from release builds. Left in, they allow any user to fabricate a streak and claim milestone rewards.

Scenario: A projected figure is presented without a returns disclaimer
Expected Behavior: Every surface that renders a forward-looking number must carry the illustrative-only disclaimer and name the assumed rate. Block release on any projection surface missing it.

Scenario: Marketing copy states 15 percent per annum without qualification
Expected Behavior: Every rate reference must carry the terms-and-conditions marker and be reviewed by compliance before release.

Module: ## CORE FUNCTIONALITY — P1 — required for the product to work as designed

Scenario: Contributions are made at 23:59 and again at 00:01
Expected Behavior: Resolve both against a local calendar day index so they count as two distinct days.

Scenario: User changes device timezone between contributions
Expected Behavior: Apply the local UTC offset before flooring to a day index so the boundary lands on local midnight rather than 05:30 IST.

Scenario: Device clock moves backwards through a manual change or westward travel
Expected Behavior: Treat a today value at or before the last contribution day as no elapsed time. Never break or penalise the streak.

Scenario: A negative day index arises from time travel or an edited store
Expected Behavior: Normalise the negative modulo before rotating so the weekday index always resolves within zero to six.

Scenario: App is left foregrounded across local midnight
Expected Behavior: Re-read the session on refresh or foreground so the day rolls over and the daily action becomes available again.

Scenario: Streak lapses while the app is closed
Expected Behavior: Reconcile the streak during session boot and emit a single streak-broken event so the user sees the outcome on first paint.

Scenario: Invest button is double-tapped
Expected Behavior: Treat the calendar day as the unit of record. Accept the contribution amount but prevent a duplicate streak increment.

Scenario: Two separate contributions are made on the same calendar day
Expected Behavior: Record both amounts against the ledger while holding the streak count at one increment for that day.

Scenario: One day is missed while a shield is held
Expected Behavior: Consume exactly one shield and preserve the existing streak count. Notify the user that a shield was spent.

Scenario: More days are missed than shields held
Expected Behavior: Reset the current count to zero, consume all held shields, and preserve the longest-run record.

Scenario: Unbroken run continues past the shield cap
Expected Behavior: Cap holdings at two shields. Additional weekly grants are not accumulated.

Scenario: Streak breaks and is rebuilt back through a milestone already celebrated
Expected Behavior: Read from the reached-milestone history so a celebration and its reward fire exactly once per milestone per account.

Scenario: Streak is rebuilt past a milestone it never actually crossed
Expected Behavior: Derive the active reward from history rather than the current count so the uncrossed milestone remains owed rather than silently skipped.

Scenario: A milestone reward is earned and the streak subsequently breaks
Expected Behavior: Hold the reward at claimed permanently. An earned reward must never revert to locked.

Scenario: Contribution write fails after a completed hold
Expected Behavior: Hold the charge indicator through the write, then drain it and surface an inline retry. The empty indicator is the signal that nothing was committed.

Scenario: Device clock is set forward several days to farm additional contribution days
Expected Behavior: Derive the current day from a server timestamp rather than the device clock, and reject contributions dated ahead of server time.

Scenario: A contribution day falls on 29 February
Expected Behavior: Day indices are derived from elapsed epoch days, so a leap day is a normal day with no special handling. Cover with a fixed-date regression test.

Scenario: A user in a DST-observing region crosses a 23-hour or 25-hour day
Expected Behavior: Compute the offset from the date being evaluated rather than a cached offset so a shortened or lengthened day still yields exactly one day index step.

Scenario: Two completion events are emitted for a single contribution
Expected Behavior: Deduplicate one-shot events by contribution identity and surface at most one event per mutation, with milestone outranking lesser acknowledgements.

Scenario: A user attempts the daily contribution while offline
Expected Behavior: Queue the contribution locally with an idempotency key and submit on reconnect so the streak is preserved. Today only the SIP commit path supports queueing.

Scenario: Clock jumps forward by many days at once
Expected Behavior: Consume shields for each covered day in a single reconciliation pass and report the total spent, rather than looping the user through repeated notices.

Scenario: A shield is earned and a milestone is crossed on the same contribution
Expected Behavior: Persist both outcomes to state and surface only the milestone. The shield count must still increment.

Scenario: App launches for the first time with no persisted state
Expected Behavior: Boot into the initial state and route to the phone step. An empty store is a valid first-run condition and must not be treated as an error.

Scenario: Phone number is entered with fewer or more than ten digits
Expected Behavior: Cap input at ten digits at the source and re-validate on submit with a distinct message per failure case.

Scenario: Phone number does not begin with 6, 7, 8 or 9
Expected Behavior: Reject before dispatch with a message naming the valid leading digits rather than failing after an OTP that never arrives.

Scenario: A repeated-digit placeholder number is submitted
Expected Behavior: Reject as an implausible number. This is the most common junk input.

Scenario: A number is pasted with spaces or a country-code prefix
Expected Behavior: Strip all non-digit characters before validating and storing.

Scenario: An incorrect verification code is submitted
Expected Behavior: Reject with a non-retryable validation error and retain the entered digits for correction.

Scenario: A digit is edited and the code re-completes while a submit is in flight
Expected Behavior: Guard against concurrent submits so verification is attempted exactly once per completed code.

Scenario: A name is entered in Devanagari, Tamil or another Indic script
Expected Behavior: Accept letters together with combining marks so scripts that build vowels from marks are not rejected.

Scenario: A name contains digits or unsupported symbols
Expected Behavior: Reject with a letters-only message while permitting apostrophes, hyphens, periods and spaces.

Scenario: An age below 18 or above 100 is submitted
Expected Behavior: Reject at both the field and the API boundary. 18 is the regulatory floor for investing.

Scenario: An unrecognised gender value reaches the profile write
Expected Behavior: Validate at the API boundary rather than trusting the client, since the value selects character artwork consumed by every later screen.

Scenario: Sign-up is abandoned mid-flow and the app is relaunched
Expected Behavior: Persist the reached step and resume at exactly that screen so a verified number is never re-collected.

Scenario: The story chapter is entered before a profile exists
Expected Behavior: Reject the purpose write with a validation error directing the user to complete their profile.

Scenario: Back is pressed part way through the story chapter
Expected Behavior: Rewind one narrative beat per press and hand control to the navigator only at the first line. Hardware back and the on-screen control must invoke the same handler.

Scenario: Back is pressed on the home screen immediately after onboarding completes
Expected Behavior: Dismiss the onboarding stack on completion so back exits the app rather than replaying sign-up.

Scenario: A remote font fails to load at launch
Expected Behavior: Boot on system faces after a bounded wait. Never block app start on typography.

Scenario: A pre-referral payload is upgraded and the accepted count is absent
Expected Behavior: Backfill the count to zero during migration so the reward ladder never performs arithmetic on an undefined value.

Scenario: App is terminated mid-commit and relaunched
Expected Behavior: Persist only user choices and the queued commit. Always re-derive transient status so no screen resumes claiming a write is in flight.

Scenario: Simulated latency exceeds the request deadline
Expected Behavior: Reject as a timeout after the deadline elapses rather than waiting indefinitely.

Scenario: A retry is attempted on an error that can never succeed
Expected Behavior: Mark validation, limit, storage, not-found and cancelled errors as non-retryable and suppress the retry affordance for them.

Scenario: A request is aborted because the user navigates away
Expected Behavior: Reject the pending delay immediately on abort with a cancelled error and detach the listener.

Scenario: Requests fail repeatedly on a flaky connection
Expected Behavior: Back off exponentially with a hard cap so the interface never appears hung.

Scenario: Time Machine loads with no network
Expected Behavior: Enter a queued-offline state that retains the last successfully fetched data and keeps on-device scrubbing fully functional.

Scenario: Connection is lost during a SIP commit
Expected Behavior: Persist the commit with its idempotency key, present a queued card naming the saved time, and submit automatically on reconnect.

Scenario: The queue is drained while still offline
Expected Behavior: Leave the queued item intact and re-attempt on the next successful load. Never send twice and never discard.

Scenario: Load is invoked again while a load is already in flight
Expected Behavior: Return early so concurrent loads cannot interleave and produce inconsistent state.

Scenario: User navigates back into the Time Machine from the success screen
Expected Behavior: Acknowledge the success on unmount so the machine returns to ready rather than resuming a completed commit state.

Scenario: Cached portfolio data is served while stale
Expected Behavior: Display the last-synced time whenever data is older than the refresh interval and dim forward-looking figures so cached values are never mistaken for live ones.

Scenario: A second SIP change is committed while one is already queued
Expected Behavior: The queue holds a single commit today, so a second overwrites the first. Replace with an ordered queue keyed by idempotency key before launch.

Scenario: Airplane mode is toggled at the moment a commit is dispatched
Expected Behavior: Resolve to exactly one terminal state — committed or queued — and never both. The user must see a single unambiguous outcome.

Scenario: Skip-months lever exceeds the whole projection horizon
Expected Behavior: Halt all future contributions while continuing to compound existing capital.

Scenario: SIP delta would drive the daily contribution below zero
Expected Behavior: Clamp the daily contribution at zero. A negative contribution would invert the invested total.

Scenario: Start year equals end year
Expected Behavior: Return a single point equal to the present balance rather than an empty series.

Scenario: A year outside the series range is requested
Expected Behavior: Clamp to the first or last point rather than extrapolating beyond the modelled horizon.

Scenario: A lever intended to help produces a worse outcome after an engine change
Expected Behavior: Assert directionality in the suite: helpful levers must raise the final value and harmful levers must lower it.

Scenario: A daily contribution stream is compounded annually
Expected Behavior: Compound monthly and emit yearly points so contributions are not treated as arriving at year end.

Scenario: Time Machine is opened on an account with no contributions
Expected Behavior: Fall back to the seeded demonstration fixture so the feature remains reviewable, and never overwrite a real holding with fixture data.

Scenario: Projected portfolio value is zero or below
Expected Behavior: Present a dedicated empty state naming the minimum daily amount rather than rendering a flat line at zero.

Scenario: A SIP commit fails outright
Expected Behavior: Keep the sheet open with an explicit statement that nothing was changed. Dismissing would conceal the failure.

Scenario: Profile daily amount or age is edited after a projection has been viewed
Expected Behavior: Recompute the series from the edited inputs on next read and invalidate any memoised entry keyed on the previous values.

Scenario: Assumed rate is changed while a lever is applied
Expected Behavior: Recompute both the base and levered curves against the new rate so the displayed delta always compares like with like.

Scenario: Two-futures comparison is opened on an account with no invested capital
Expected Behavior: Fall back to the demonstration fixture or present the empty state. Never render two identical flat lines as a comparison.

Scenario: The late-start comparison is read as a prediction
Expected Behavior: Label both paths as illustrative, name the assumed rate inline, and describe the delay as a modelled scenario rather than a forecast.

Scenario: Borrow screen is opened with nothing invested
Expected Behavior: Present an empty state explaining that borrowing is secured by the portfolio rather than a live screen quoting a zero limit.

Scenario: Accrued interest is read on the day a loan is taken
Expected Behavior: Floor the elapsed-day count at zero so interest begins at zero and never computes negative.

Scenario: Selling appears cheaper than borrowing in the comparison
Expected Behavior: Price both futures from the same engine and the same horizon so the comparison is internally consistent and reproducible.

Scenario: Requested amount exceeds remaining capacity but capacity is above zero
Expected Behavior: Offer the maximum permitted amount as a partial borrow rather than rejecting outright, and state the shortfall explicitly.

Scenario: Available borrowing capacity is exactly zero
Expected Behavior: Disable the action, label it as no remaining capacity, and explain what would increase it.

Scenario: A loan is repaid while a contribution streak is active
Expected Behavior: Repayment must not alter the streak, the contribution ledger or Future You standing. No repayment flow exists today.

Scenario: Projections are read immediately after borrowing
Expected Behavior: Recompute the projection with the loan recorded: portfolio value is unchanged because units are not sold, and accrued interest is disclosed separately.

Scenario: Multiple concurrent loans are outstanding
Expected Behavior: Sum principal and accrue interest per loan against its own origination day. Aggregate loan-to-value across all outstanding principal.

Scenario: Portfolio value falls so that loan-to-value breaches the ceiling after the fact
Expected Behavior: Block further borrowing, disclose the breach, and define a margin policy before launch. No margin call path exists today.

Scenario: A single large deposit is made on day one
Expected Behavior: Gate every evolution stage on both consistency and capital so a stage cannot be reached by deposit alone.

Scenario: A long streak is held with negligible invested capital
Expected Behavior: Hold the stage until both the consistency and capital thresholds are cleared.

Scenario: Progress is requested for an account far ahead on one axis and behind on the other
Expected Behavior: Report the lower of the two axes and name which one is binding so the next action is unambiguous.

Scenario: A streak break or withdrawal drops the account below its current stage threshold
Expected Behavior: Define the regression policy explicitly. Recommended: retain the highest stage ever reached as a permanent record and present current standing separately, so progress is never seen to be revoked.

Scenario: Artwork is missing for a newly added expression key
Expected Behavior: Resolve every asset statically at bundle time so a missing file fails the build rather than rendering a blank frame at runtime.

Scenario: Feed is rendered for an account with no invested capital
Expected Behavior: Switch copy to an invitation to start. Never report growth on an empty portfolio.

Scenario: Growth is read on a day the user has just contributed
Expected Behavior: Exclude the same-day deposit from booked growth. Capital moved is not money earned.

Scenario: Feed is rendered before a purpose has been chosen
Expected Behavior: Fall back to the default goal target so the funded percentage never divides by an undefined value.

Scenario: Portfolio value exceeds the goal target
Expected Behavior: Cap the displayed funded percentage at 100, mark the goal complete, and offer the next target rather than rendering a figure above 100 percent.

Scenario: The user revisits the story chapter and selects a different purpose
Expected Behavior: Recompute the goal target and funded percentage immediately, and disclose that the target changed so the percentage movement is explained.

Scenario: A user wants to track more than one goal
Expected Behavior: Only a single derived goal is supported. Scope multiple concurrent goals with independent targets and progress before advertising the capability.

Scenario: A completed goal is reopened or the target is raised
Expected Behavior: Preserve the completion record and present progress against the new target from the existing balance rather than resetting progress to zero.

Scenario: The same number is stored in different formats across sessions
Expected Behavior: Normalise to the final ten digits before deriving the code so one number always resolves to one code.

Scenario: Consecutive phone numbers sharing a prefix generate codes
Expected Behavior: Distribute codes so that at least 495 of any 500 consecutive numbers produce distinct values.

Scenario: All referral tiers have been earned
Expected Behavior: Return no next tier and hold progress at complete. Do not render a phantom further rung.

Scenario: An invite link is opened on a device without the app installed
Expected Behavior: Route to the store and preserve the code through install via deferred deep linking so attribution survives the first launch.

Scenario: An invite is redeemed after the programme window closes
Expected Behavior: Attach an explicit expiry to each issued code and reject redemption past it with a clear message to both parties.

Scenario: A referred user uninstalls or closes their account after the reward is credited
Expected Behavior: Define a clawback and qualification window — for example the reward vests after the invitee's seventh contribution — and present the pending state until it vests.

Scenario: A pending invite is cancelled by the inviter
Expected Behavior: Support revoking an outstanding invite and reflect the change in the ladder count within the same session.

Scenario: A share is initiated with no active streak
Expected Behavior: Render a distinct first-day card and caption. Never publish a zero-day claim.

Scenario: A shared card is forwarded without its caption
Expected Behavior: The image alone must carry the streak claim, the product name, the mechanism and both rates.

Scenario: A screen reader user reaches the year scrubber
Expected Behavior: Expose an adjustable role with minimum, maximum and current values plus increment and decrement actions. Drag must not be the only means of operation.

Scenario: System font size is set to the largest accessibility setting
Expected Behavior: All monetary figures, labels and calls to action must remain fully legible without truncation or overlap at the maximum supported scale.

Scenario: A screen reader traverses the home screen
Expected Behavior: Announce elements in a deliberate reading order — balance, then streak, then the daily action — with the primary action reachable without traversing the carousel.

Scenario: Text and interface colours are measured against contrast standards
Expected Behavior: Every text and essential interface colour pair must meet at least 4.5 to 1 against its background. Tertiary text and green-on-dark require audit and remediation.

Scenario: A screen reader user attempts the press-and-hold contribution
Expected Behavior: Provide an equivalent single-activation path on the streak screen. A timed hold gesture cannot be performed under an assistive touch interface.

Scenario: A screen reader user reaches the projection chart
Expected Behavior: Provide a text alternative summarising start value, end value and the selected year. A canvas with no alternative is unreadable.

Module: ## EXPERIENCE QUALITY — P2 — degrades the product but does not block release

Scenario: Time Machine preference blob is corrupt
Expected Behavior: Fall back to default preferences without entering an error state. Defaults are fully usable.

Scenario: Preference write fails during a scrub commit
Expected Behavior: Swallow the failure. The user loses a preference, not data, and the screen must remain interactive.

Scenario: Week strip is rendered for any week including one containing a negative index
Expected Behavior: Always resolve to seven contiguous days beginning on the Monday on or before the given day, never in the future.

Scenario: Every milestone has been earned
Expected Behavior: Return no active reward and hold milestone progress at complete so the ring reads as finished.

Scenario: Screen is unmounted while a hold is in progress
Expected Behavior: Clear the haptic interval on unmount so a dismissed screen cannot continue emitting feedback.

Scenario: A milestone is crossed from a screen other than the streak page
Expected Behavior: Mount the celebration above the navigator so it presents wherever the contribution originated.

Scenario: Several one-shot events qualify from a single contribution
Expected Behavior: Rank milestone above shield-earned above plain acknowledgement and present exactly one.

Scenario: Reconciliation runs more than once within a single session
Expected Behavior: Reconciliation is idempotent for a given day index, so repeated runs produce no additional shield spend or state change.

Scenario: A monetary value above five digits is rendered
Expected Behavior: Apply Indian digit grouping so magnitude is read correctly, without relying on locale support that varies across runtimes.

Scenario: A projection is requested at a zero percent annual rate
Expected Behavior: Guard the annuity division so the result is the linear sum of contributions rather than a division by zero.

Scenario: A contribution made today is valued
Expected Behavior: Return the principal unchanged for a non-positive elapsed-day count.

Scenario: A contribution below the product minimum is posted
Expected Behavior: Reject with a validation error naming the minimum daily amount.

Scenario: A daily amount outside the supported band is set
Expected Behavior: Clamp is not applied; reject with a validation error naming both bounds so the user chooses explicitly.

Scenario: A position sits at the maximum permitted loan-to-value
Expected Behavior: Draw the utilisation bar against the ceiling rather than against 100 percent so a maxed position reads as full.

Scenario: A long scrubbing session spans many rates and lever combinations
Expected Behavior: Bound the memoisation cache and evict least-recently-inserted entries so memory cannot grow without limit.

Scenario: The scrubber is dragged continuously
Expected Behavior: Return the memoised series for unchanged inputs so the gesture sustains 60 frames per second.

Scenario: A scrub gesture is cancelled by a parent scroll view
Expected Behavior: Commit on gesture finalisation rather than on end so the committed year can never diverge from the knob position.

Scenario: Data lands after the loading state
Expected Behavior: Match skeleton block geometry to the arriving layout so no content shifts on transition.

Scenario: The JavaScript thread is busy during a load
Expected Behavior: Drive the skeleton pulse on the UI thread so the shimmer continues while work is in progress.

Scenario: A negative day offset is supplied to the demo clock
Expected Behavior: Clamp the offset to zero and round to a whole day.

Scenario: An account with no history has a streak of zero
Expected Behavior: Treat broken as zero current with a non-zero longest run, so a new account is never presented as having failed.

Scenario: The two character sets ship at different native crops
Expected Behavior: Read the true aspect ratio per character set so neither is distorted by a shared frame.

Scenario: Character artwork has no alpha channel
Expected Behavior: Paint the sampled backdrop colour behind the image and feather the outer edge into the page so no rectangle is visible.

Scenario: Feed copy is generated for a zero streak
Expected Behavior: Present the streak row as starting today rather than as continuing.

Scenario: Emergency cover is expressed in months
Expected Behavior: State the assumed monthly expenditure wherever the figure appears so no decision rests on an undisclosed assumption.

Scenario: A cohort comparison is presented to the user
Expected Behavior: Present a documented band derived from published retention curves and label it as indicative rather than fabricating a precise per-user figure.

Scenario: Several feed rows are opened in succession
Expected Behavior: Keep exactly one row expanded at a time so the surface remains scannable.

Scenario: Progress is requested at the highest evolution stage
Expected Behavior: Guard the zero-width span and return complete with no binding constraint.

Scenario: An invite code is read aloud
Expected Behavior: Exclude visually ambiguous characters from the code alphabet.

Scenario: A code is requested with no stored phone number
Expected Behavior: Fall back to a deterministic seed and still return a valid six-character code.

Scenario: The invite code is tapped to copy
Expected Behavior: With no clipboard module in the dependency set, route through the share sheet and confirm the action in the label.

Scenario: The platform share sheet is unavailable or refused
Expected Behavior: Degrade to sharing the caption as plain text rather than failing the action.

Scenario: Photo library permission is denied
Expected Behavior: Present a plain explanation that there is nowhere to save the image. Do not re-prompt within the same session.

Scenario: The media library module is absent from the runtime client
Expected Behavior: Fall through to the system share sheet, which includes the photo library as a destination.

Scenario: A messaging application target is not installed
Expected Behavior: Detect the unavailable handler, state it plainly, and open the system share sheet instead.

Scenario: The user dismisses the share sheet without sharing
Expected Behavior: Treat dismissal as a neutral outcome. Do not present an error.

Scenario: A negative streak value reaches the export filename
Expected Behavior: Floor and round the value so the generated filename is always valid and stable per streak.

Scenario: A field is auto-focused and blurs before the user types
Expected Behavior: Reveal validation only after the field has been meaningfully touched so an untouched field is never marked wrong.

Scenario: The resend control is activated repeatedly
Expected Behavior: Gate resend behind a 30 second countdown and clear both the entered code and any prior error on each resend.

Scenario: A name longer than the supported length is pasted
Expected Behavior: Enforce the maximum at the field and reject at validation with the limit named.

Scenario: A full date of birth is pasted into the age field
Expected Behavior: Restrict the field to three digits so an over-long paste cannot be accepted.

Scenario: The story question is presented on a short device
Expected Behavior: Cap the option list height and allow it to scroll so the character remains fully in frame.

Scenario: A development reload occurs while the splash screen is being dismissed
Expected Behavior: Catch both prevention and dismissal rejections so a reload cannot take the app down.

Scenario: The account menu is opened on a narrow device
Expected Behavior: Constrain panel width to the screen minus its gutters so no edge is clipped.

Scenario: A menu row is selected while the dismiss animation is running
Expected Behavior: Defer the navigation until the dismissal has begun so the two transitions do not contend for the same frame.

Scenario: A new consumer subscribes to the store with an inline selector
Expected Behavior: Require selectors to return a stable reference and define them at module scope so identity is preserved across renders.

Scenario: A contribution is made while several screens are mounted
Expected Behavior: Scope subscriptions per state slice so an unrelated slice does not re-render.

Scenario: A shared animation value is mutated by the component it was passed to
Expected Behavior: Retain ownership in the hook and pass the value read-only.

Scenario: An accordion chevron rotation is driven during render
Expected Behavior: Drive the animation from an effect so no shared value is written during a render pass.

Scenario: A card navigates to a destination that is already a mounted tab
Expected Behavior: Navigate rather than push so a duplicate instance of a mounted tab is not stacked.

Scenario: The reduce motion accessibility setting is enabled
Expected Behavior: Disable auto-advancing content entirely and suppress decorative scale and spring animations.

Scenario: System haptics are disabled or unsupported
